sections.title: Page 2

summary.text: Sets out the draft resolution on the rational use of drugs, which thanks participants of the Nairobi expert conference and asks all parties, from governments and industry to prescribers and consumers, to take on the responsibilities set out in the Director-General's summing up. It also asks wealthier Member States to help developing countries and requests the Director-General to carry out the revised drug strategy, seek extra funding and report back to the Executive Board and the Forty-first Assembly.

summary.text: Opens the resolution on infant and young child feeding, recalling earlier Assembly resolutions and noting that, five years after the International Code of Marketing of Breast-milk Substitutes was adopted, unsuitable products are still promoted for infants. It welcomes guidelines on when infants must be fed on substitutes and urges Member States to apply the Code and involve health professionals, NGOs, consumer groups and industry in protecting breast-feeding.

sections.title: Page 4

summary.text: Continues the infant feeding resolution, asking Member States to obtain monitoring information from manufacturers, report on Code implementation and supply breast-milk substitutes in hospitals through normal procurement rather than free or subsidized supplies. It asks the Director-General to propose a standard reporting form and to stress that early feeding of other foods can undermine breast-feeding and that so-called follow-up milks are unnecessary.

sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: Sets out the resolution on acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, which endorses the Director-General's report, expresses concern at the spread of LAV/HTLV-III infection and urges Member States to cooperate under WHO coordination, share information and put prevention strategies in place. It asks the Director-General to keep supporting countries, seek extrabudgetary resources and report to the Fortieth World Health Assembly.

sections.extract: ACQUIRED IMMUNODEFICIENCY SYNDROME Having considered the report of the Director-General on WHO activities for the prevention and control of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome Concerned with the continued increase of LAV/HTLV-III infection and AIDS in many parts of the world; Mindful of the long-term requirements for action in this area and of the need for additional resources as well as international cooperation;
